description.narrative: The Program Development Objective (PDO) is to increase the coverage of primary health care for underserved populations and improve the efficiency of health spending by addressing underlying institutional challenges.

The development objective of the Health Program for Results Project for Romania is to increase the coverage of primary health care (PHC) for underserved populations and improve the efficiency of health spending by addressing underlying institutional challenges. The program scope is informed by the findings of analytical work and the experiences of previous engagements and defined by the country's demand and application of the country partnership framework (CPF) filters. The program focuses on three results areas in which the government requested the Bank's support and where the Bank's engagement is likely to make a significant impact: results area 1: improving PHC coverage for underserved populations; results area 2: rebalancing the hospital-centric system toward effective PHC; and results area 3: improving health expenditure efficiency by addressing critical cost drivers.

title.narrative: At least 50% of patented medicines positively assessed through the new HTA methodology receive conditional reimbursement decisions

comment.narrative: On track. Development of the new HTA methodology is ongoing. Technical assistance is being provided to update the HTA methodology, in line with standards outlined by the NHIH and the MoH. The new methodology is expected to be completed by November 2025. Once complete, the associated legislation will be drafted and publicly consulted, after which the legislative approval process will begin, with approval expected by December 2025 by Ministerial Order. Once the legislation is approved, reimbursement for patented medicines positively assessed should begin to increase within four months.

title.narrative: Proportion of supplies and devices for emergency medical services (in value) procured under framework agreements

comment.narrative: On track. The Emergency Ordinance on centralized procurement was approved in 2024. An Action Plan for the period January 2025-April 2026 was agreed and includes the approval of 238 items (medical supplies and devices) to be procured centrally and organized into 88 distinct products (variations in size and use) and grouped into 71 lots. The first batch of procurement includes 104 items (44%) and is expected to be completed in early 2026. The second batch includes 91 items (82%) and is expected to be completed by the Program closing date.

title.narrative: Number of community health care workers (community health nurses and Roma health mediators) trained

comment.narrative: Achieved. Training has been provided to all community health care network (1,946 community health care workers and 468 Roma mediators) on usage of the upgraded version of the AMCMSR App. Beyond this, another training course was conducted for 158 community health workers (and up to 350 community health care workers who covered personally the training fee) as part of the POCU project. A subsequent POIDS (EU/Managing Authority for the Inclusion and Social Dignity Programs) project that covers training of 2,000 community health care workers and Roma health mediators is expected to be held in July 2025. There are already 150 collaboration protocols concluded between the community health centers and PHC providers. In September 2025, there are 500 integrated community health care teams ready to start the work.

title.narrative: Percentage of National Health Insurance House's annual budget allocated to PHC (Percentage, Custom)

comment.narrative:
On track. The NHIH PHC budget was 9.6% in 2023, triggering the achievement and disbursement of DLI 3. The PHC expenditure in 2025 was 3% higher than forecasted due to the impact of reforms related to the scope of service packages and provider-payment mechanisms that entered into force in July 2023 and had a full year of implementation. For 2025, the initial PHC expenditure is 2.5% higher than in 2024 due to stability in the scope of the service packages and tariffs; the share in total NHIF expenditure for health services is measured at 7.6%.
The decrease in NHIH annual budget allocation between from 9.6% in 2023 to 7.7% in 2024 and 7.6% in 2025 is deceiving - in 2023, the overall expenditure increased substantially, due to the introduction of new services and tariff increases. However, tariffs were frozen in 2024 and many providers reached service ceilings in both 2024 and 2025, resulting in a shift in the ratio despite nominal increases in financing year-on-year.

title.narrative: Percentage of National Health Insurance House's annual budget allocated to PHC (Percentage, Custom)

comment.narrative: Achieved. The share of the expenditure for PHC grew nominally in 2023 and 2024 (+13% y/y and +45% y/y, respectively). The actual expenditure on PHC in 2025 was 3% higher than forecast under the Program's expenditure framework due to the impact of reforms related to the scope of service packages and provider-payment mechanisms that entered into force in July 2023 and had a full year of implementation. As a result, while in 2023 the initial PHC budget was 25% higher than the executed budget, in 2024 the executed value was 43% higher than the initial budget (the executed PHC expenditure in 2024 was RON 5.3 billion or US$ 1.15 billion equivalent or 7.7% of the total National Health Insurance Fund expenditure for health services). For 2025, the initial PHC expenditure is 2.5% higher than in 2024 due to stability in the scope of the service packages and tariffs; the share in total NHIF expenditure for health services is measured at 7.6%.
